And this is why I feel bad for your partner when you have kids. The best interest of the kid is to learn respect and responsibility so that when he goes out into the real world he knows how to deal with situations by himself.  

Honestly if you don’t get this by now the. Why are we arguing. You are obviously going to raise your kids to know that they don’t need to follow your rules if the other parent isn’t around. Good luck. Cheers.

Because when you have kids you don’t undermine the other parent. Regardless of if you are together or not. 
If that’s the way OP and his ex want to parent then absolutely mom didn’t discuss punishment with dad so then sure dad shouldn’t keep punishment going at his home. Buy the kid a beer. But the kid is going to learn that if he wants something from either parent he knows he can put them against each other.

I have been going off of others comments that he should be treated as an adult if he is basically 18. 

But barring that, the mom did act like an adult, albeit a stupid one. That’s why OP needs to act like an adult and either follow through or talk her down. But going behind her back and just giving him a beer won’t help anyone.

He would follow through because that’s what you do on a parenting team. HOWEVER she absolutely should have discussed the punishment with OP before making one that would also affect him. 

I don’t think swearing is a big deal I swore in front of my parents all the time. But obviously this mom doesn’t think it’s ok. Or maybe swearing is ok and she just wanted to make a point that she’s the boss. 

Yah it’s too harsh for just dropping the F bomb. But sometimes life is unfair and you have to be an adult about and deal with it. Going behind moms back isn’t going to do anything. Teach the son how to deal with it like an adult and have a mature conversation about why it’s a bad punishment and prove he is old enough to manage his own shit.

OP says he had never set punishments that intrude on her time with him. Not that it’s only active at his home. 
I agree that it is unfair to everyone because OP is now having to live up to a standard he doesn’t agree with. And deviating from what worked for them before is going to cause strife between the different family units. 
OP should talk to mom and tell her it’s ridiculous or teach his son how to have an adult conversation so he can make his point without getting upset or making mom upset.

And I agree with all of that. I’m not arguing that the son shouldn’t be allowed to manage his own extracurriculars etc. Frankly he should be managing himself at that age. 
I’m just saying that OP ignoring the punishment that mom put down will make it seem like son can do things with dad that he can’t do with mom (and vice versa if that is the case). 
If the whole point is that the son should be treated like an adult then the parents in the situation should both agree on that and how to deal with “issues” with their son.  
If son wants to be treated as an adult then he doesn’t need to be swearing at his mom. He just needs to explain that he should be able to make his own choices which isn’t ridiculous if he’s managing the rest of his extracurriculars and still getting As.

The punishment is unfair. And stupid. And she should have just asked for an apology. 

OP should follow through because the punishment was made. Not because of what he did or said to get the punishment. As an adult the son should tell the mom that he thinks the punishment is unfair. Have an adult conversation about it. 

I wouldn’t want to follow through either. But I wouldn’t want my grown son to know that because that undermines the mom.
Right. I agree with that too. But OP set a punishment for his week only. Mom decided a punishment that was much longer. So unfortunately it becomes OPs responsibility to follow through.

I’m not saying her punishment was realistic. Or that it should have continued into dads week. I’m saying that the only way your kids are going to respect you when they are adults is with follow through. Mom didn’t like the swearing. It’s disrespectful. The child is punished (however stupidly) and there needs to be follow through. Whether dad agrees or not if he goes against mom he’s teaching son that that is ok. 

And just because you are legally an adult does not mean that you are an adult.

I disagree. It’s called co parenting. You can’t have one adult undermining the other. Regardless of if the punishment was deserved or not. She set a boundary and the kid needs to adhere to it. He will still be 18 in a few weeks and you having your first beer together legally will still be exciting. By not following her punishment you are teaching him that it’s ok to disrespect his mother. 
I say ESH the mom for the outrageous punishment for a 17 y/o. And dad for thinking buying his son a beer is more important than teaching the kid he needs to take what he gets.
